newsitem.title: USA: US steel rod makers file dumping charge with ITC.
newsitem.headline: US steel rod makers file dumping charge with ITC.

text.p: Four U.S. steel rod producers and a union group filed an unfair trade case with the Department of Commerce and the U.S. International Trade Commission on Wednesday over the "dumping" of rod imports from seven countries, the U.S. Specialty Steel Industry said.

The petition charged that stainless steel rod imports from Italy, Germany, Japan, Korea, Spain, Sweden and Taiwan are being sold in the United States at prices well below the product's home market value -- a practice called dumping.
The petitioners requested that the U.S. government impose antidumping duties ranging up to 46 percent on the imports of stainless steel rods from those countries.

"The U.S. industry has faced a surging growth of imports in recent years, with overall import penetration at 70 percent in 1996 and about 68 percent today. Much of the growth has been achieved through foreign unfair trade practices such as dumping and government subsidization," a spokesman for Specialty Steel Industry said in a statement.

The petitioners account for virtually all stainless steel rod production in the United States and include the following: Al Tech Specialty Corp, Carpenter Technology Corp, Republic Engineered Steels Inc, Talley Metals Technology Inc and the United Steelworkers of America union.
